name: Isolated Hereditary Congenital Facial Paralysis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Isolated Hereditary Congenital Facial Paralysis

criteria.description: Facial paralysis present at birth or within the first month of life
Positive family history of isolated facial nerve paralysis consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
No associated neurological deficits or systemic abnormalities
Electroneurography or electromyography showing facial nerve dysfunction without other cranial nerve involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital facial paralysis with positive family history and absence of other neurological or systemic abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by family history and electrophysiological studies; genetic testing may assist but no specific gene identified universally.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral or bilateral congenital facial nerve paralysis
searchTerms: one or both sides facial nerve paralysis from birth
congenital facial muscle weakness
birth-related facial nerve palsy

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absence of facial muscle movement in affected regions
searchTerms: no movement of facial muscles in area
loss of facial muscle function
unable to move parts of face
uneven facial expression at rest
asymmetric face when relaxed
one side of face looks different
incomplete eyelid closing
eyelids do not fully shut
lagophthalmos causing eye exposure

common.symptomName: Difficulty with feeding due to impaired lip seal
searchTerms: difficulty feeding due to lip weakness
trouble sucking from poor lip seal
feeding problems from lip muscle issues

common.symptomName: Hypoplasia of facial muscles on affected side
searchTerms: underdeveloped facial muscles on one side
weak muscles on one side of face
reduced muscle bulk in half of face

occasional.symptomName: Synkinesis or involuntary facial muscle contractions
searchTerms: involuntary facial muscle movements
uncontrolled facial twitching

occasional.symptomName: Mild hearing impairment due to associated middle ear anomalies

slight hearing difficulty due to middle ear issues
partial hearing impairment related to ear structure

occasional.symptomName: Dry eye syndrome secondary to incomplete eyelid closure
searchTerms: dry eyes from incomplete eyelid closure
eye dryness due to blinking problems
irritated eyes from eyelid not closing fully
difficulty speaking clearly
trouble pronouncing words
speech problems

rare.symptomName: Facial bone hypoplasia on affected side
searchTerms: underdeveloped facial bones on one side
smaller bones in half of face
facial bone growth deficiency on affected side
mild learning or growth delay
slight developmental slowing
some delay in milestones

rare.symptomName: Secondary corneal ulceration due to exposure keratopathy
searchTerms: corneal ulcers from eye exposure
eye surface sores due to dryness

imaging: MRI or CT may show hypoplasia of the facial nerve canal or absence of facial nerve nucleus
Facial muscle hypoplasia on imaging studies
genetic: No single causative gene identified; genetic heterogeneity suspected
other: Electroneurography demonstrating reduced or absent facial nerve conduction
Electromyography showing denervation of facial muscles

distinguishingFeatures: Involvement of multiple cranial nerves (VI and VII)

redFlags: Progressive worsening of facial paralysis after birth
Signs of systemic or syndromic involvement
